about.title: About Ideal Weight Calculator
about.description: The Ideal Weight Calculator provides reference weight estimates using multiple established formulas including Devine, Robinson, Miller, and Hamwi methods. These calculations use inputs such as height, gender, and body frame to show a range of formula-based results. Use the output as a general reference rather than a personal medical recommendation, since body composition, muscle mass, and individual factors can affect interpretation.

faq.q: How should I interpret the ideal weight formulas?
faq.a: No single ideal weight formula works equally well for everyone. The calculator shows multiple formula outputs so you can review a range of results rather than relying on one number. Consult healthcare professionals for individualized guidance.

faq.q: How do I determine my body frame size for the calculator?
faq.a: Measure your wrist circumference at the narrowest point. For women: <6 inches = small frame, 6-6.25 inches = medium frame, >6.25 inches = large frame. For men: <6.5 inches = small, 6.5-7.5 inches = medium, >7.5 inches = large frame.

faq.q: Should I aim for a single target weight number?
faq.a: Ideal weight calculators provide general guidelines, not a personal target. Focus on a healthy weight range while considering body composition, muscle mass, and overall health. The range is usually more useful than one formula result.

faq.q: Do ideal weight formulas work for athletes and muscular people?
faq.a: These traditional ideal weight formulas may not reflect athletes with high muscle mass, because they do not account for body composition differences. Athletes and very muscular individuals should focus on body fat percentage and broader health markers instead.

faq.q: What's the difference between ideal weight and healthy weight?
faq.a: Ideal weight formulas provide mathematical estimates based on height and gender. Healthy weight is a broader concept that includes factors like body composition, fitness level, and overall health. Our calculator helps estimate ideal ranges, but healthy weight varies individually.

faq.q: How does age affect ideal weight calculations?
faq.a: Most traditional ideal weight formulas don't factor in age, but metabolism and body composition naturally change with age. Older adults may have slightly higher healthy weight ranges. Consider age-related factors when interpreting calculator results.
